text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers:
- An agreement on workers' benefits is expected to be signed late this week or at the begining of next, government, employers, and trade unions said after they successfuly finished talks on Tuesday.

- No progress in succession talks could be expected until principle of five equal successor states is accepted, said Miran Mejak, head of Slovenia's delegation, attending former Yugoslavia's succession talks in Brussels.
- Slovenian Defence Minister Tit Turnsek on Tuesday visited U.S. Secretary of Defence William Cohen in order to gain support for Slovenia's joining NATO in the first round of its expansion.
- Investments rose to 26.15 billion tolars ($166.9 million) in April, a 7.8 percent increase from the same month last year, Slovenian Payment Agency said.
- In the last seven years percentage of smokers among Slovenian population dropped to 26 percent from 32 percent, a medical survey showed.
- Slovenian producer prices in April rose 0.4 percent compared to March and 6.2 percent compared to the same month last year, the country's statistical office reported on Tuesday.
- The Bank of Slovenia is expected to talk about ending the reconstruction of two Slovenia's largest state-owned banks Nova Ljubljanska Banka and Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor.
